title: The maker of non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch
key_facts: TypeSafe AI, developer of the Jev model, raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation.
The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Sequoia and existing investor DCVC taking part.
Jev was released on 15 September 2026 and went viral almost at once.
Jev is built on a transformer architecture but is not a large language model; it outputs probabilities the company calls "calibrated decisions".
The company claims a third of Fortune 500 companies already use the model.
The company says Jev works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than LLMs.
TypeSafe was co-founded in 2024 by Diogo Almeida (formerly OpenAI), Sasha Sheng (formerly Meta) and Erik Gafni.
quote_evidence: TypeSafe AI, the developer of Jev, a new type of AI model that gained rapid popularity after launching just a few weeks ago, has raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation.
The startup claims that a third of Fortune 500 companies are already using the model, a remarkably swift adoption by enterprises.
It doesn’t output text, but instead produces probabilities, or what the company calls “calibrated decisions.”
why_it_matters_hint: A model aimed at automating tasks rather than writing text drew a very large round within weeks of release.
event_date: Round reported 9 Oct 2026; Jev released 15 Sep 2026
notes: Adoption and speed figures are company claims, not independently checked.
